gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Bose's own battery footnote on the QuietComfort Ultra (2nd Gen) US page measured 24 h with Immersive Audio off and 18 h with it on at 75 dB loudness, against the 30 h / 23 h headline, while Apple's 20 h is rated at 50% volume and RTINGS measured the Sony WH-1000XM6 at 31.75 h with ANC on.
standout_why: SoundGuys' cited best list (updated Oct 19/30, 2026) gives no battery hours at all for the XM6, QC Ultra 2nd Gen or AirPods Max 2, no quick-charge figures and no test conditions; SoundGuys' compare page and both What Hi-Fi pages (which I could not open: 403/truncated) are, per ChatGPT's summary, repeating the 30 h / 30 h / 20 h / 60 h maker headlines. None mention Bose's 24 h / 18 h footnote, the 75 dB vs 50% volume difference between Bose's and Apple's test conditions, or that Sony's spec sheet lists a passive 'headset turned off' cable mode while SoundGuys lists 'No USB listening' for Sony and 'USB-C lossless' for Bose and Apple.
decides: Confirms Sony WH-1000XM6 as the pick for long trips: its one third-party measurement (RTINGS 31.75 h) beats the number Bose itself measured for the QC Ultra 2nd Gen (24 h, or 18 h with Immersive Audio on), so ChatGPT's 'Bose for long flights' framing rests on a headline figure Bose's own footnote undercuts. It also flags a real trade: Sony is the only one of the three that lists a wired mode with the headset powered off, but it is the only one of the three with no USB-C audio, which Bose (16-bit/44.1 or 48 kHz) and Apple (lossless) both offer.
